newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North says may make U.S. bond issue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North says may make U.S. bond issue.

text.p: Diversified resources group North Ltd said on Friday it may go to the U.S. debt market for between US$200 million and US$300 million to replenish debt faciltiies used to take a stake in Iron Ore Co of Canada (IOCC).

"There is some very attractive longer term money there for us, possible beyond 10 years. We'd probably be going for US$200 million US$300 million," executive director, finance, Julian Vear told Reuters.

North earlier announced it was paying US$230 million to take a 59.3 percent stake in IOCC. Vear said the purchase would be funded from US$550 million worth of revolving credit facilties signed with banks in September last year.

"We can handle all of the purchase price with cash from our existing facilities," he said. Vear said North also would consider extending the bank debt facilties was an alternative option to the U.S. bond issue but no decision had been made.
Vear said North would wait for an upgrade in its credit rating from agency Moody's Investors Service before committing to the U.S. issue.

"We believe we've got a pretty good chance of getting the Moody's rating upgraded and that would give us a better price inthe bond market so we would rather go to the bond market when we know where we stand ... which will probably be in a few months," he said.
North's U.S. debt issues are currently rated Baa2 by Moody's which the company says is two levels below its Standard & Poor's Corp offshore rating of A-minus.
